intent: Kept: five sensors at x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12. Changed: mass from 0.8 to 0.75 kg and body_length from 0.18 to 0.16 m, the midpoint inertia the Integrator proposed (about 20 percent below the baseline, about 37 percent above iteration 4). Expected result: oval and s-bend progress rise above the iteration-5 values (oval about 0.55 to 0.6, s-bend about 0.14 to 0.2), slalom line loss stays at or below about 0.2, and the score is 112 to 125. Under consideration, not committed: if slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher, hold the baseline (mass 0.8, body_length 0.18) and stop reducing inertia. If it is at or below 0.1, the next step is a controller-only test, since the Integrator's feedback says the inertia lever is then used up.
learning: Iteration 9 confirms the wheel_track 0.12 platform as the baseline (111.80, slalom line loss 0.10). max_error at 0.061 to 0.066 m across all geometries looks like the run-ending threshold, so I track progress and slalom line loss as the scoring signals. The open question is whether the midpoint inertia buys progress without pushing slalom line loss past 0.2.
rationale: Iteration 9 reproduced the iteration-5 platform (wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, sensors at y 0.03, 16 mm footprints, span ±0.06 m) and scored 111.80, identical to iterations 1 and 5. Slalom line loss was 0.10, so the baseline is confirmed. The narrow-track tests (iterations 6 to 8, scores 72.9 to 79.6) were all worse, with slalom line loss up to 0.35 and oval progress halved, and they did not reduce max_error. I am keeping wheel_track 0.12. The Integrator's feedback (entityR1) asks, on a reproduced 111.8 with slalom line loss at or below 0.1, for the midpoint inertia test with the controller unchanged. I am taking that advice. Iteration 4 (mass 0.7, body_length 0.14) gave the best progress (oval 0.53, s-bend 0.20) but slalom line loss of 0.85. Iteration 5 (mass 0.8, body_length 0.18) gave slalom line loss 0.10. Yaw inertia m(L²+W²)/12 is about 0.00312 at the baseline, 0.00250 at the midpoint and 0.00198 at iteration 4. So the midpoint sits roughly halfway, and I expect it to recover some progress while keeping slalom line loss below the 0.2 stop rule. The risk is that slalom line loss rises well above 0.1, and the Integrator has said not to go below this midpoint. Sensors, span, footprint, wheel radius and body width are unchanged, so the race isolates inertia.
